known_issues: BT pairing flaky on Windows 11 Home — use USB-BT dongle if onboard radio misbehaves.
notes: STN2100 superset of ELM327. Shop favorite for multi-make work; handles pre-2011 Harley J1850 reliably, unlike most ELM327 clones.

known_issues: Counterfeit ELM327 — firmware usually reports v2.1 but is actually v1.5 silicon. Drops frames on 500 kbit CAN. J1850 support claimed but does not work.
notes: Cheapest option available, ~$13 shipped. Works for basic Mode 03 on modern CAN bikes. Avoid on Harley, avoid for bidirectional actuation. Sold under 50+ brand names (Vgate, Veepeak, BAFX, etc.).

known_issues: WiFi pairing breaks after hotspot changes. Same underlying counterfeit ELM327 silicon as the BT clone. Keep-alive watchdog resets session every ~60s on some firmware.
notes: Same firmware quality problem as the BT variant — just with a different radio. Slightly more convenient for iOS users (BT ELM327s require a paid app like OBD Fusion).

known_issues: FTDI/CH340 chip knockoffs — driver install on Windows 11 requires disabling driver signature enforcement for the cheapest variants.
notes: USB variant of the generic clone. More stable session than BT/WiFi (no wireless drops) but shares the same counterfeit ELM327 firmware problems.

known_issues: STN1110 slightly slower than MX+'s STN2100 on multi-frame CAN reads; noticeable on Mode 22 PID bursts. Otherwise rock-solid.
notes: Mid-tier ScanTool product. Real STN1110 silicon (not an ELM327 clone). Excellent value for shops that don't need the MX+'s peak throughput.

known_issues: USB-only; no wireless option. Linux support via usbserial requires kernel 5.x or newer for reliable USB CDC enumeration.
notes: Entry-level STN1110 — same silicon as LX in USB form. Shop-bench favorite for laptop-tethered diagnostics where wireless is unwanted.

known_issues: ELM327 v1.5 silicon (slightly more selective QC than the $13 clones but still counterfeit). J1850 intermittent; avoid for Harley work.
notes: The least-bad ELM327 clone. BAFX does actual inventory QC so the adapter you receive tends to work; no J1850 support despite the spec sheet claim.

known_issues: BLE stack occasionally needs a power-cycle to reconnect. Mode 22 absent despite some marketing suggesting otherwise.
notes: BLE 4.0 variant — better battery impact than the old BT 2.x Vgate units. Good travel/app-pairing option; not a shop-bench workhorse.

known_issues: Marketed for Ford/Mazda cars — motorcycle support is possible but not the primary use case. HS-CAN + MS-CAN switching requires the FORScan app UI.
notes: STN1110-based with FORScan-optimized firmware. Bidirectional works on cars; motorcycle bidirectional support varies by model.

known_issues: Autel's iOS/Android app is the only way to unlock bidirectional — no raw AT-command passthrough. Motorcycle coverage is limited vs their car database.
notes: Consumer-grade Autel dongle. Good bidirectional car support, partial bike support. Annual software renewal required for full feature set.

known_issues: Standalone scanner — no PC/phone connection. Read-only by design; no bidirectional. Limited motorcycle-specific menus.
notes: Shop-bench handheld. Rugged, works without batteries/phones. Good for quick code pulls on a generic OBD-II bike; not suitable for deep HD-specific diagnostics.

known_issues: Harley-only. Tune slots are consumed on each ECU flash; buying a second-hand PV3 often means the slots are already used (unlock costs ~$100).
notes: Pro-grade Harley tuning + diagnostic tool. Full bidirectional (idle-set, A/F trim, knock test, actuator sweep). Works on pre-2011 J1850 and 2011+ CAN Harleys. Industry standard for Harley tune shops.

known_issues: EFI controller + diagnostic hybrid — replaces the stock Delphi ECM on pre-2011 Harleys. Not a plug-and-play OBD scanner; installation requires full wiring integration.
notes: Aftermarket EFI replacement with built-in datalogger. Pro-level Harley tuning tool. Listed here for completeness — mechanics who run Twin Tec typically pair it with a laptop via their proprietary USB interface, not OBD-II.

known_issues: Harley 2007-present only. Requires VIN unlock per bike via the V&H app; swapping between bikes costs a re-flash.
notes: Harley-specific Bluetooth flasher + diagnostic. Full DTC read/clear + live data + auto-tune pairing with V&H slip-ons. Strong alternative to Dynojet PV3 for shops that run V&H exhaust.

known_issues: Harley-only, smaller vendor (support responsiveness varies). Android app mandatory — no iOS.
notes: Mid-range Harley-specific scanner. Full bidirectional including idle relearn, fuel trim, TPS reset. Popular in independent HD shops for shops that don't need Dynojet's tuning features.

known_issues: Unofficial clones of the Harley-Davidson dealer tool. Firmware quality varies wildly by seller; eBay units often ship with out-of-date firmware. No official update channel.
notes: Clones of the OEM HD dealer tool (DTII, MAT-II). Real dealer access to security-gated functions (key reprogramming, immobilizer sync, ABS bleed). Legal gray area — MoCo actively discourages. Listed for reference; recommend authorized dealer service for these operations.

known_issues: Authorized HD dealers only. Requires annual subscription + Digital Technician II software license. Not available to independent shops via retail channels.
notes: Factory dealer tool — reference only. Full access to all HD diagnostic + security functions. Independent shops cannot legally purchase new units; listed as the 'gold standard' baseline.

known_issues: Simulator / test only — not a real adapter. Phase 144 scenario engine exposes this entry so tests can wire a compat row to the simulated bike fleet.
notes: Reserved slug for the Phase 144 MockAdapter / SimulatedAdapter bridge. Do not purchase — this is the motodiag in-memory test harness, not a shippable product.

known_issues: BLE-only — classic-Bluetooth Windows apps (older OBD II scanners) do not pair with it. iOS works natively; Android works via the OBDLink app.
notes: iOS-focused STN2100 unit. Same silicon as MX+ in BLE form. Mechanics who scan on iPhone/iPad choose this over MX+; classic-BT shops stick with MX+.

known_issues: Mostly marketed for cars/trucks. Motorcycle coverage is generic OBD-II only; make-specific menus are absent. Firmware update process is cumbersome (proprietary PC app).
notes: Budget handheld. Works for basic DTC read/clear on OBD-II-compliant bikes. No PC/phone connection option; truly a standalone device.

known_issues: Launch's motorcycle database is a paid annual add-on. Without it, only generic OBD-II works — no make-specific interpretation.
notes: Shop-bench handheld from Launch (major Chinese diagnostic brand). Good display + navigation; motorcycle add-on database is the real value unlock.

known_issues: BimmerCode bundle is BMW-coding focused — motorcycle features require the BMW Motorrad coding profile (separate in-app purchase).
notes: MX+ hardware paired with the BimmerCode/Motorcycle app. Best consumer option for BMW R1200GS / S1000RR coding work. Hardware is identical to plain MX+ — the value is the software bundle.

known_issues: Authorized Ducati dealers only. Annual subscription + training certificate required.
notes: Factory Ducati dealer tool. Full access to Panigale / Monster / Multistrada diagnostic and service functions. Listed for reference — independent shops need to use an STN2100-based aftermarket option (MX+ with coding app) for comparable depth.

known_issues: Authorized Kawasaki dealers only. Windows laptop with KDS software required; proprietary cable bundle ships with the kit.
notes: Factory Kawasaki dealer diagnostic. Full ZX / Ninja / Versys service menu including ECU update + immobilizer pairing. Reference-only for independent shops.

known_issues: BMW-only (plus a few Husqvarna models built on BMW platforms) - useless on any other make. Consumer/Enthusiast tier is VIN-limited: service functions are unlocked for 10 stored VINs, after which HEX wants the Professional upgrade or the ProUnlimited annual subscription (~$99/yr). Two incompatible physical connectors: round 10-pin for pre-2017 bikes, OBD-II for 2017+ EU4 bikes - buying the wrong one means an adapter cable. WiFi mode drives a cloud-hosted app from phone/tablet, so a dead internet connection in the shop degrades you to the USB/PC path. Newest model-year coverage tracks HEX firmware/software releases and can lag the bike's release.
notes: The de facto independent-shop BMW Motorrad tool. Reads BMW proprietary ECU/ABS/ESA/immobiliser fault codes that generic ELM327 hardware cannot see at all, and runs real service routines: service reminder reset, ABS/integral-brake bleed, throttle/idle adaptation reset, actuator activation, live sensor data. Sold as GS-911wifi (WiFi + USB, PC/Mac/iOS/Android) and a cheaper USB-only Gen 2 (PC only, ~$330). Recommend it over any BimmerCode/OBDLink combination when the job needs BMW service functions rather than coding - the OBDLink path covers coding and generic CAN, the GS-911 covers the dealer-style service menu. For a shop touching more than 10 BMWs, budget for Professional/ProUnlimited from the start.

model: TuneECU (Android) with KTM 6-pin Sumitomo B6AP to OBD-II adaptor
known_issues: Keihin-era KTMs only, and TuneECU's own bikes list says unlisted bikes are not compatible: no 125/200/250/390 Duke or RC (Bosch), no 790/890/990 Duke or Adventure (Bosch), no EXC TPI/TBI two-strokes, no Euro 5 model of any family. Two physical paths: the K-line bikes (990 LC8, 1190 RC8, 690 to 2013, 250/350 SX-F) need a USB KKL FTDI cable (adaptor type C), while the CAN bikes (690 from 2014, 1050/1090/1190/1290 Adventure, 1290 Super Duke) use an ELM327-class or OBDLink Bluetooth adapter (adaptor type D) — both through the same third-party 6-pin-to-OBD-II adaptor. Function set is narrow on the CAN bikes: fault codes, live data and actuator tests only, no map read/write and no adjustments of any kind. The developer documents connection-stability problems on some KTMs, especially with the engine running (COM-port settings, cable shield to ground, ferrite choke); a reseller warns later KTMs often fail to connect. Windows version discontinued. Price shown is the EUR 25 Standard licence (1 year, 5 bikes) converted at time of writing; hardware adaptor and interface are extra (roughly GBP 12 to 30 from UK resellers). Pro licence EUR 300 / 3 years.
notes: The independent-shop tool for Keihin-managed, pre-Euro 5 KTMs, distributed as a direct APK from the developer's site rather than an app store. Per TuneECU's Basic guide, by model: 990 LC8 and 1190 RC8 — map read/write over USB, actuator tests (fuel pump, SAI, second throttle, O2, injector, coil), reset engine adaptation and the throttle-cable adjustment; 690 Duke 3 and 690 SMC/Enduro/Supermoto to 2013 — map read/write over USB, tests, reset engine adaptation only; 250/350 SX-F — diagnostics and tests only; 690 Duke 4, 690 from 2014, 1050/1090/1190/1290 Adventure and 1290 Super Duke (all not Euro 5) — Bluetooth only, diagnostics and tests, no adjustments. TuneBoy (Australia) lists twelve older KTMs but as a tune-editing and data-logging kit, not diagnostics. For Bosch-era and Euro 5 KTMs the options are KTM's PC-based dealer tool or dealer-level third-party scanners that list KTM by model.

model: TuneECU (Android) for Triumph — 16-pin socket, no adaptor
known_issues: Android only; the Windows build is discontinued. Coverage is defined by engine-management generation and frame-number break rather than by model year, so a machine near a boundary must be checked by frame number — the published breaks are the authoritative discriminator and the year ranges here are mapped from them. Map write and service reset need a USB KKL 409.1 FTDI cable on some models and a specific Bluetooth adapter on others; the function set differs per model in the published matrix, so confirm the exact bike before promising a function. Carburetted air-cooled machines are outside any tool's scope because they have no engine control module at all. Licence price is not published on the vendor site (bought in-app); the figure here is the commonly quoted standard licence converted at time of writing and should be treated as indicative rather than a vendor price.
notes: The diagnostics-capable independent tool for Triumph, with a published per-model function matrix spanning both the Sagem-managed bikes (Daytona T595/955i, Speed Triple T509/955i, Sprint ST/RS 955, Tiger T709/955i, Speed Four, TT600) and the later Keihin ones (air-cooled Bonneville 865 family through the modern range). Functions per the vendor's own matrix: read and clear fault codes, live sensor values, actuator tests, reset engine adaption, throttle position reset, reset service interval, and map read/write. Connects directly to Triumph's 16-pin socket — the vendor's guide lists the marques that need an OBD-II adaptor and Triumph is not among them. Euro 5 machines with the red 6-pin connector need a 6-pin-to-16-pin adapter.

model: DealerTool for Triumph (Windows) — third-party, not Triumph's own software
known_issues: Third-party product despite the name — this is NOT Triumph's own dealer software, which is the separately distributed Triumph Diagnostic Tool available only through Triumph's dealer portal. Windows only, and requires the vendor's own modified interface cable. Service reset is explicitly not supported on a published exclusion list that includes the Trident, the 660 models generally, the Tiger Sport 800 and several recent models — check the current list before promising that function. Throttle balance without gauges is unavailable on the Sagem-managed and four-cylinder Keihin machines. Bikes from approximately 2023 need a 6-pin-to-16-pin adapter. Prices are the vendor's own in GBP; the figure here is converted at time of writing and is indicative. The vendor site is client-rendered, so a plain fetch of any path returns a shell — the coverage and function statements are on its FAQ and purchase pages.
notes: Covers fuel-injected Triumphs broadly, from the earliest Sagem-managed machines through the current Keihin ones, with fault codes and descriptions, code clearing, live sensor values, dealer-level diagnostic tests and a throttle balance performed without vacuum gauges. The strongest single diagnostic answer for the injected air-cooled Bonneville family, which had no adapter coverage in this catalog before Phase 230. Not a tuning product — map flashing is not among its functions.

model: PADS (Piaggio Advanced Diagnostic System) — Aprilia dealer channel
known_issues: Obtainable only through a Piaggio Group dealer agreement, so it is not purchasable by an independent workshop; price is therefore recorded as zero rather than as a figure. Aprilia's own Service Station Manual directs the reader to the dealer interface to reset ECU errors, so some resets have no documented alternative. The PADS acronym expansion rests on a tool vendor's page rather than on Piaggio's own documentation.
notes: Aprilia's factory tool. Named here so the catalogue records what the dealer route actually is; independents should look to TuneECU, GuzziDiag or OBDSTAR for the accessible subset.

model: IDC5 / IDC6 BIKE with Navigator TXB interface
known_issues: TEXA publishes no price, so the figure here is zero rather than an invented one; cost is an interface plus a recurring software subscription rather than a one-off purchase. Coverage is claimed at make level and this project could not verify that three-cylinder and four-cylinder MV families are covered equally — confirm the exact model before purchase.
notes: MV Agusta's OFFICIAL dealer tool, not merely an aftermarket option: a 2012 MV press release states all authorised service centres worldwide would adopt the TXB, and TEXA's own release notes list MV AGUSTA among makes that chose IDC5 as their official tool. Uniquely among exotic makes, MV's dealer tool and the best independent tool are the same product.

model: GuzziDiag / IAWDiag (free) with FTDI K-line cable
known_issues: The software is free; the price recorded is a typical cable set, which is the only thing actually purchased. Covers Magneti Marelli ECU families (IAW 5AM, 59M, 15M, 15P, 15RC, 7SM, MIUG3, MIU, MBC1) rather than a model list, so coverage follows the ECU fitted and must be checked per machine. Windows-oriented and unsupported in the commercial sense.
notes: The genuinely free route into Marelli-equipped Aprilias. Cable sets are sold specifically for 2009-2020 RSV4 and 2011-2020 Tuono V4 — two of the very few manufacturer- or vendor-stated year ranges available for this make.

known_issues: OBDSTAR publishes per-model coverage only as downloadable coverage lists rather than on the product page, so no row here is coverage-list verified and all are make-level only. Confirm the specific model and year with the vendor before purchase.
notes: Dedicated Aprilia handheld: code read and clear, live data, action tests, coding, service reset. The most capable independent option that is a single purchase rather than a subscription.

known_issues: Per-model coverage is published only as a downloadable list, so rows here are make-level and not coverage-verified. MV runs three-cylinder and four-cylinder families with different control unit configurations and no source consulted confirms parity between them — do not assume the triples and the fours are equally covered. Ships with 4/3/2-pin MV adapters plus a separate Euro 5 adapter.
notes: Code read and clear, live data with record and playback, action tests, coding, instrument coding, maintenance reset and ABS control unit setting.

model: TuneECU (Android/Windows) with Aprilia 3-pin or 6-pin OBD2 adaptor
known_issues: PRIMARILY A MAPPING TOOL, NOT A CODE READER. TuneECU's own guide documents map read/write (USB only), fuel pump, injector and coil tests, Reset TPS, Handle Self Learning and Throttle Self Learning for Aprilia — but shows no per-model fault-code read and clear screen, so DTC capability on this make is unconfirmed rather than established. An OBD2 adaptor is required IN ADDITION to the cable or Bluetooth interface, which is easily missed when ordering. MV Agusta is absent from the supported marque list entirely.
notes: The self-learning functions are the real value for a workshop: throttle and handle self-learning are routinely needed after throttle body or sensor work and are otherwise a dealer visit. Price shown is a typical adaptor lead.
